AccessApprovedRequest.description: Decision response of an approve call: requester-private projection (no requester identity) after the decision. decided_by and decided_at are always set, and the applied membership grant is always present.

AccessApproverRequest.description: Approver queue projection. Ineligible requester email and display name are both redacted to null; submitted workspace name stays a frozen snapshot.

AccessBudgetWindow.description: One budget window as a platform reader sees it: usage is always visible. Three shapes: known (no unknown-cost request; remaining_microusd is a decimal), unknown (at least one unknown-cost request: every figure is present but remaining_microusd is null) and unavailable (the accounting row is unreadable: used_microusd, unresolved_usage, exhausted, settled_microusd, pending_held_microusd, unknown_held_microusd, unknown_cost_requests and remaining_microusd are all null together and headroom_status is unknown). A null group therefore implies headroom_status unknown, but unknown does not imply the null group (governance/totals.rs read_budget_report and BudgetReport::remaining, policies.rs budget_windows).

AccessDeniedRequest.description: Decision response of a deny call: requester-private projection (no requester identity) after the decision. decided_by and decided_at are always set; a denial never carries a membership grant.

models.description: At most the first 10 distinct model names (alphabetical); model_count is the full distinct count.

token.description: One-time invitation value; returned only at creation. Never an example, URL, log entry or list field.

AccessMapping.description: Two closed variants mirroring the oidc_group_mappings CHECK constraint (0001_enterprise.sql): target_kind platform requires platform_role and no workspace fields; target_kind workspace requires workspace_id and workspace_role and no platform_role.

diff.description: email is never null: preview rows exclude cleaned-up users (lifecycle.rs preview_platform_effect/preview_workspace_effect: usr.cleaned_at IS NULL) and an immediate row names only unrevoked grants, which cleanup revokes before clearing the address. A row is `gained` when the after rank is above the before rank (so after is never null) and `lost` when it is below (so before is never null)

digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored mapping (directory.rs mapping_digest), the value a later If-Match must quote.

immediate.description: The management write's own immediate effect, present with applies:true only when the write would revoke grants (a delete, or a merge that changes a field).

oneOf.description: No stored grant changes (an unchanged merge): the default of evaluate().

diff.description: email is never null: preview rows exclude cleaned-up users (lifecycle.rs preview_platform_effect/preview_workspace_effect: usr.cleaned_at IS NULL) and an immediate row names only unrevoked grants, which cleanup revokes before clearing the address. A new mapping can only add access: grants are compared with the existing ones, never removed (existing_mapping_id is null), so the *_lost lists are always empty.

digest.description: A preview of a NOT-YET-SAVED mapping has no stored state to confirm, so the digest is always null.

immediate.description: A not-yet-saved mapping has no grants to revoke; the evaluator's fixed default (group_mapping_preview.rs).

email.description: Never null: a cleaned-up user's grants are all revoked before the address is cleared (lifecycle.rs cleanup_user), and the member list only returns unrevoked grants.

source.description: Team/Project rows only: the personal 'personal' source is filtered out by the platform export query (subject_export.rs, kind IN ('team','project')).

AccessPlatformMapping.description: A platform-role group mapping: platform_role set, every workspace field null.

AccessSessionId.description: Client session label (X-Session-Id): 1-128 characters, no control characters, no leading or trailing whitespace (inference::client::valid_session_id).

AccessWorkspaceAccess.description: Workspace-scoped effective access (GET /workspaces/{ws}/access): no key is bound, so key_id is null, the key layer is the inactive stub (applies=false, null limits/budgets/catalogs/restriction), and the key layer and the key_restriction reason are never emitted. Reason layers are platform (model-level facts), type_default, workspace_override or workspace; budget reasons carry the period.

models.description: At most 200 models, ordered by public name: the handler reads 201 rows, returns the first 200 and sets truncated (access.rs).

AccessWorkspaceContext.description: Personal owner-private projection omits object_visibility entirely. A platform reader may see only shared metadata, with no membership role.

AccessWorkspaceMapping.description: A Team or Project workspace-role group mapping: workspace_id, workspace_role (admin or member) and the live workspace name and kind set, platform_role null.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Shared management handler envelope, not a universal framework response. code equals the HTTP status string. Selected reasons add period, limit, missing_meters or retry details. Detail keys are closed over the inventoried handler vocabulary (policy period/limit, price missing_meters, and access/key-issuance retry details).

IdentityAdminCeilingNotification.description: Even Platform Admins never receive a personal workspace identity: personal=true forces workspace=null and a null/absent workspace_name. Non-personal references are Team/Project only.

IdentityAdminSummaryBudgetVisibility.description: Closed administrative projection: workspace-wide budgets visible.

IdentityCeilingDetails.description: Exact alerts::ceiling_conditions producer fields and wire types. workspace_name is nullable for personal events and omitted by non-Admin redaction; every other producer field is required. No workspace id, nested workspace or owner identity is permitted.

IdentityExportProfile.description: Profile of the signed-in person. Every export sits behind a verified browser session, and the only session writer (identity.rs callback) stores first/last_signed_in_at in the same statement, so both sign-in times are never null. disabled_at and platform_role stay NULLABLE: verify_session (identity.rs:1442) checks them in its own pool statement, and subject_export reads PROFILE (subject_export.rs:147) later in a separate snapshot after recording the audit event (:174-175), so a disable or role revocation in between is observable as a non-null disabled_at or a null platform_role. email is nulled only by account cleanup (lifecycle.rs), which subject_export PROFILE excludes.

anyOf.x-omg-unobserved-branch: The request is authenticated by verify_session (identity.rs:1442, a pool statement requiring users.disabled_at IS NULL) and the profile is read later in a separate snapshot (subject_export.rs:175 and :147), so only an administrator disabling the person in that window yields a timestamp; a test cannot interleave the two statements.

verify_session (identity.rs:1442) joins effective_platform_roles, but PROFILE (subject_export.rs:147) reads the role in a later snapshot, so a role revoked in that window yields null; a test cannot interleave the two statements.

IdentityFailure.description: Management handler envelopes and identity middleware's actual string-valued error are distinct wire contracts.

IdentityMemberSummaryBudgetVisibility.description: Closed member/redacted projection: workspace-wide budgets are always null.

display_name.description: models.display_name is NOT NULL DEFAULT '' (0001_enterprise.sql); an unnamed model is the empty string, never null.

details.$comment: Stored alert_events.details is an arbitrary producer-specific JSON object; monetary and identity refinements remain enforced.
details.description: Stored JSON incident payload, not a serde DTO. Fields vary by producer/kind; readers do not deserialize or close this map. Every *_microusd value is a non-null integer micro-USD string (unknown cost is reported in unknown_cost_requests, never as null). Each alerts.rs producer field is typed individually: pending_microusd is sum(held - held_unknown) read from budget_totals with no sign guard (migration 0015 has no >= 0 check), so drifted accounting can make it negative and it is signed; used_microusd (an incident needs used to reach a positive threshold of a positive reference), budget_microusd, spend_amount_microusd and min_spend_microusd (validated positive amounts), and current_microusd, baseline_total_microusd and baseline_hourly_microusd (settled ledger sums, CHECK(actual_microusd >= 0)) are unsigned. Any other *_microusd value from a producer not listed must still be an integer string (signed form). Admission-ceiling identity redaction is constrained by the separate variants below.

IdentityOwnAccessRequest.description: Requester-private projection: no requester_email or requester_display_name. The workspace name is the submitted snapshot, not its current discoverability/name.

IdentityRedactedCeilingNotification.description: Non-Admin projection of a non-personal event: no workspace identity/name, including nested details. A personal event carries no identity for any audience and matches only the personal branch of IdentityAdminCeilingNotification, keeping the oneOf exclusive.

IdentitySignedDecimal.description: Exact integer micro-USD that may be negative: governance totals::read returns settled+held with no non-negativity guard, so drifted accounting can report a negative string.

IdentityUnsignedDecimal.description: Exact nonnegative integer; money fields are micro-USD, never floating point.

IdentityWithdrawnAccessRequest.description: A withdrawn request. Always decided by the requester at the time of withdrawal and never linked to a membership grant: access_requests CHECKs (0066_access_requests.sql) require status='withdrawn' to carry decided_by=requester and a non-null decided_at, and only approved requests have an access_request_applications row. Requester-private projection: no requester_email or requester_display_name.

parameters.description: Opaque: send only a next_cursor returned by a previous page of the same filters. Today it is '<last-activity microseconds since the epoch>_<workspace uuid>_<hex of the UTF-8 session id>'. The handler (logs.rs session_cursor) splits at the first two underscores, parses the first part as a signed 64-bit integer (a leading '+' is accepted) that must be a representable timestamp, parses the second with uuid::Uuid::parse_str (which also accepts the simple, braced and URN spellings), and requires an even-length hex third part of at most 1024 hex characters that decodes to a valid session id; anything else is 400. The schema pattern admits only the form the gateway emits (hyphenated uuid, no '+', at most 19 digits) and cannot check the 64-bit or timestamp range or the decoded session id.
